knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.2.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly distinguishes a prediction interval from a parameter confidence interval?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the future-observation vs parameter contrast.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Prediction intervals cover future data; parameter CIs cover parameters. Prediction intervals are typically wider because they include process/residual variation as well as parameter uncertainty.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Prediction interval → future observation; parameter CI → unknown parameter.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating the two interval types as interchangeable, or claiming prediction intervals are narrower.

choices.label: A prediction interval targets a future observation using a model fitted to a random sample. A parameter confidence interval targets an unknown parameter, not the future observation itself.
A prediction interval and a parameter confidence interval always cover the same numerical object; only the name changes.
A prediction interval is always narrower than the corresponding parameter CI because a single future observation has less uncertainty than a mean.
A prediction interval estimates only the sampling variance of an estimator and never involves residual or process variation.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.2.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. You fit a model to historical annual losses and need an interval for next year's loss Y_new. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Prediction vs parameter CI; refuse mean-CI-as-prediction.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Prediction targets Y_new; a CI for E[Y] targets the mean. Proper prediction intervals account for both parameter uncertainty and process variation.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Prediction interval covers Y_new; a CI for E[Y] does not substitute.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Using a mean CI as if it covered the next observation.

choices.label: A prediction interval aims to cover the future observation Y_new (parameter uncertainty plus process/residual variation). A confidence interval for E[Y] covers only that mean parameter and does not finish the prediction-interval task.
A confidence interval for mean loss already covers Y_new with the same coverage probability, so no separate prediction interval is needed.
A prediction interval covers E[Y] only; covering Y_new would require a parameter confidence interval instead.
Prediction intervals ignore parameter uncertainty and use only the residual variance from a fitted model with parameters treated as known exactly.
